cards.question: What types of tests exist and what does each verify?
cards.answer: Unit tests verify individual functions or components in isolation. Integration tests verify that multiple units work correctly together. End-to-end tests verify complete user workflows in a real browser. Static analysis (TypeScript, ESLint) catches errors at compile time.
keyPoints: Unit: fast, isolated, test one function or component at a time
Integration: real interactions between components, services, DB
E2E: full user journeys in a real browser — highest confidence, slowest
Testing pyramid: most unit, some integration, few E2E

cards.question: What are the core Jest APIs?
cards.answer: describe groups related tests. test/it defines a single test case. expect creates an assertion. Lifecycle hooks (beforeEach, afterEach, beforeAll, afterAll) handle setup and teardown. jest.fn() creates mock functions, jest.mock() replaces entire modules.
keyPoints: toBe for primitive equality (===), toEqual for deep object equality
jest.fn() mocks functions, tracks calls and arguments
jest.mock('./module') replaces module with auto-mocked version
beforeEach/afterEach run around each test for setup/cleanup

cards.question: What query priority does React Testing Library recommend?
cards.answer: Queries should match how users find elements. Prefer accessible queries: getByRole, getByLabelText, getByPlaceholderText, getByText. Fall back to getByTestId only as last resort when no semantic query is possible.
keyPoints: getByRole is most preferred — mirrors assistive technology
getByLabelText for form inputs
getByText for static visible content
getByTestId only as last resort — tests implementation detail

cards.question: What is the difference between stubs, mocks, and spies?
cards.answer: A stub replaces a function with a simple fixed response (no behavior verification). A mock replaces a function and also verifies it was called with expected arguments. A spy wraps the real function, tracking calls without replacing behavior. In Jest, jest.fn() can act as all three.
keyPoints: Stub: fixed return value, no call verification
Mock: fixed return + verify how it was called
Spy: wraps real function, observe calls without replacing it
jest.spyOn(obj, 'method') creates a spy on an existing method

cards.question: How do you test asynchronous behavior?
cards.answer: Use async/await in tests to handle Promises. React Testing Library's findBy queries wait for elements to appear. Use waitFor for arbitrary async assertions. Avoid arbitrary delays — always wait on a specific condition.
keyPoints: async/await for Promise-based assertions
findByX = waitFor + getByX shorthand — prefer for async UI
waitFor retries until assertion passes or times out
Never use arbitrary wait times — tests become slow and brittle

cards.question: How do you write maintainable Playwright tests?
cards.answer: Use the Page Object Model (POM) to encapsulate page interactions in dedicated classes, separating test logic from page implementation details. Use data-testid attributes for stable selectors. Record failures with screenshots and traces. Test only critical user journeys.
keyPoints: Page Object Model: each page/component gets a class with interaction methods
Stable selectors: prefer data-testid or ARIA roles over CSS selectors
Record screenshots and traces on failure for debugging
Keep E2E tests focused on critical paths — they are expensive to maintain
